residents.cold: Cold at the window. The set warms the right hand, the stove warms the left. Between them I almost qualify as comfortable.
residents.heat: Window open, receiver turned down. Everyone else's summer is coming through perfectly.
residents.wet: Rain on my sill. Very regular. I can tune out most regular things. This one needs a towel.
residents.snow: Snow at the window. The street has lost its high notes. I turned the set down to hear the difference.
residents.clearing: The rain has stopped hitting my sill. I keep waiting for the next drop. Apparently that is listening too.
residents.fair: A little sun on the receiver. Makes the dust visible. Unfair advantage, sunlight.
residents.trend: Several days of it now. One begins adjusting the room instead of the weather forecast.
residents.fog: The roof across the way has gone into the fog. Still hear the street. Much cheaper than a view.
residents.night: The window is dark now. The set makes the room seem lit even with its lamp turned down. I should probably turn it down.

residents.cold: Cold comes in under the door. I'm taking the sunny side on the next run. Adds half a block. Worth it.
residents.heat: It's close in here. Next delivery goes by the shady side, even if the address is on the other one.
residents.wet: Rain at the window. That means tram rails like soap. Straight across them, never along. Ask my elbow.
residents.snow: Snow. Fine going downhill until you remember the bottom of the hill is still there.
residents.clearing: Stopped raining. Good. There's about ten minutes when everyone else is still deciding whether to go out.
residents.fair: Clear patch over the roofs. I could get three errands done before anyone finishes describing it.
residents.trend: Third day of this sort of weather and I've changed the route twice. The street hasn't moved. Feels like it has.
residents.fog: Fog at the window. Next run is lamps and bells, no guessing where the kerb went.
residents.night: Night at the window. Next run is the lamp side of the street. You learn where the holes are, but I prefer seeing them.

residents.cold: Cold by the window. A coat on a chair warms neither the chair nor the child. I used to explain that daily.
residents.heat: The room is too close for a lesson. Unfortunately the weather is not an acceptable written excuse.
residents.wet: Rain again at the pane. Wet cuffs first, wet exercise books second, an explanation third. The order never varied.
residents.snow: Snow. Children can count flakes indefinitely and remain unable to count to twelve when required.
residents.clearing: The rain has stopped. Notice the tense. Has stopped is an observation. Will stop is an ambition.
residents.fair: Good light today. You may read by the window without blaming your handwriting on the season.
residents.trend: Several days alike do not make a rule. They do make a useful opening sentence. Put the dates beside it.
residents.fog: Fog today. If you cannot see the far side, say so. A guess is not an observation.
residents.night: Dark outside. An excellent time to finish the page before putting the book away. I am suggesting an order, not a bedtime.

residents.cold: Cold light on the wall. People call it blue. It's the orange beside it that's doing the work.
residents.heat: This heat makes the whole room yellow. I've put the yellow away. It was becoming an accomplice.
residents.wet: Wet brick beyond the glass. Finally a red that doesn't look as if it's asking permission.
residents.snow: Snow throws light up under everything. The ceiling looks as if somebody has turned the picture over.
residents.clearing: That first light after rain is indecent. Everything looks freshly painted and none of it has earned it.
residents.fair: There's a good patch of sky over the roofs. I've been avoiding it. Too easy to make it the whole painting.
residents.trend: Same light for days. I've mixed it three times. The wall hasn't changed; that's the annoying part.
residents.fog: Fog. The roofs are borrowing the colour of the sky. I wish they would do it less convincingly.
residents.night: The window has gone dark. The room is painting itself onto the glass. A rather better composition than I expected.

residents.cold: Cold enough by the window to keep my tea cold. That sentence began with a complaint and achieved a circle.
residents.heat: Too hot to finish a sentence. Too hot to start another. There, I've managed two excuses.
residents.wet: Rain against the pane. I wrote 'persistent' and crossed it out. The rain hasn't taken the hint.
residents.snow: Snow. It makes a street look finished. Briefly. No, that's unfair to the street.
residents.clearing: The rain stopped before I found an ending for it. I could simply write that down.
residents.fair: Fine light. An excellent morning for work, which is a terrible thing for a morning to be.
residents.trend: Weather repeats itself for days and nobody calls it a failure of imagination. I'm trying to learn from that.
residents.fog: Fog has removed the end of the street. A useful effect, if it would leave the beginning alone.
residents.night: Night outside. The window is a black page with this room written on it. No, that sounds finished. Leave it alone.

residents.cold: Cold window, warm valves. The room's got two climates and one blanket. I'm routing myself through the blanket.
residents.heat: It's hot enough in here without the recorder. I switched it off. Yes, voluntarily. Don't make a ceremony of it.
residents.wet: Rain on the sill: good attack, terrible sustain. No, I haven't recorded it. I put a basin under it.
residents.snow: Snow at the window. Natural noise reduction. Terrible access to the roof, lovely everything else.
residents.clearing: Rain's off. The room keeps the rhythm another minute. That's probably my foot.
residents.fair: Clear sky. Could take a cable up to the roof and waste an afternoon very efficiently.
residents.trend: Same weather for days. You'd think it could manage a second take. Not everything needs a second take.
residents.fog: Fog at the glass. Roof work can wait. Even I like knowing where the edge is.
residents.night: Night at the window. Fewer windows lit across the way. I could be considerate and turn the volume down before somebody asks.

residents.cold: Cold comes through that window like it owns the seam. Sit away from it. Tea's warmer over here.
residents.heat: Hot in here. Linen sticks, wool sulks, and people ask whether I can let out the weather an inch.
residents.wet: Rain at the window. Leave the wet coat where it can drip. A good lining remembers being dried badly.
residents.snow: Snow. Bring me the loose button before you need the coat, not while you're standing in the snow.
residents.clearing: Stopped raining. Give the coat time. You can't hurry a wet seam by looking disappointed at it.
residents.fair: Good drying weather at last. Everything on that chair is going near the window. You can take the other chair.
residents.trend: Days of this and the same clothes keep coming back damp. Tea first. Then we find something dry.
residents.fog: Fog again. Hang the coat by its loop, please. Everything feels damp enough already.
residents.night: Dark outside. Leave the coat where you can find it in the morning. Sit. There is still tea.

residents.cold: A cold draught, very confidently fitted. The window's putty is younger than the glass and ages less gracefully.
residents.heat: Close weather. Silver survives it better than its owners, provided neither is handled unnecessarily.
residents.wet: Rain at the pane. Water finds the most expensive part of a room with no knowledge of its provenance.
residents.snow: Snow outside. It lends the roof an excellent finish. I should want to inspect what it covers before bidding.
residents.clearing: The light after rain is kind to bad gilding. Kindly do not appraise anything until the pavement dries.
residents.fair: A clear light through old glass. The waviness is in the pane. Dealers are inclined to call it atmosphere.
residents.trend: Several days of the same weather. Consistency is valuable. I should nevertheless welcome a less thorough specimen.
residents.fog: Fog hides the far roofs. I decline to admire workmanship I cannot see.
residents.night: Night at the glass. Electric light is charitable to a surprising amount of bad workmanship. Mine included, occasionally.

residents.cold: Cold at the glass. I moved the cutting back a hand's width. A small distance, if you're the one moving it.
residents.heat: The leaves are losing water faster than the roots can send it up. Shade first. More water isn't always more care.
residents.wet: Rain outside. The pot inside still needs checking. Plants don't read the weather through glass.
residents.snow: Snow on the sill. The cutting knows only the cold coming through. We are the ones admiring the view.
residents.clearing: The light's back. I'll leave the cutting where it is today. No need to move a thing every time you hope for it.
residents.fair: Good light. A little sideways growth is all right. Something living needn't stand at attention.
residents.trend: Weather's settled into a habit. I check the soil, not the habit. You can be right about the season and wrong about one pot.
residents.fog: Fog at the window. The cutting is still inside. Its soil wants checking, not a weather report.
residents.night: The cutting has had its light for today. Nothing to be gained by keeping it up to watch me worry.

residents.cold: Cold coming through the frame. That's a joint, not a season. The notice will say joint.
residents.heat: This heat makes a poor room plan an immediate argument. Air needs a route. People need the same consideration.
residents.wet: Rain at the window. If water comes through a joint, tell me which joint. 'The whole building' is difficult to draw a circle around.
residents.snow: Snow on the sill. Don't bank it against a threshold. An exit doesn't cease to be an exit because it's white.
residents.clearing: Rain's stopped. Useful time to look at the marks it left. A dry wall is no alibi.
residents.fair: Fair weather. Excellent. Someone will tell me the window never leaked at all.
residents.trend: Several days make a pattern. Write where and when. A complaint with dates is much harder to put in the wrong drawer.
residents.fog: Fog outside. The street has boundaries whether you can see them or not. Mind the kerb.
residents.night: Dark outside. Keep the landing lamp on. A well-drawn stair is no use to a person who cannot see the tread.

residents.cold: Cold pane, warm room. Move the object away from the pane, rather than warming it quickly. The distinction matters.
residents.heat: The room is warm. Objects tolerate that poorly when someone keeps opening a sunny window to improve matters.
residents.wet: Rain at the glass. No, I don't propose polishing the damp off a surface that hasn't been identified.
residents.snow: Snow reflects a great deal of light. The curtain is partly drawn for a reason. The view will survive.
residents.clearing: Brightening. A sudden improvement in the weather need not become a sudden change in this room.
residents.fair: A pleasant light. Please keep the paper out of it. Pleasant is not a conservation category.
residents.trend: Steady weather for days. Easier to observe a change in the room when the conditions stop changing around it.
residents.fog: Fog. Damp air is still air; it does not remain politely on the other side of an open window.
residents.night: The window is dark. The curtain can stay drawn. Not everything in a room has to be presented to the street.

residents.cold: Cold through the window. Putty first, latch second. Turning the boiler up won't repair a gap.
residents.heat: Hot room. The fan moves air; it doesn't make cold. People bring them down as though the weather were a worn bearing.
residents.wet: Rain on the sill. Keep the set back from it. A towel isn't insulation.
residents.snow: Snow. Good time to find a draught. Bad time to discover you've painted the latch shut.
residents.clearing: Rain's stopped. Leave anything wet disconnected. 'Stopped raining' and 'dry inside' are separate conditions.
residents.fair: Clear outside. I'll take a look at the window putty while I can feel my fingers.
residents.trend: Same conditions for days. Useful. If the fault changes anyway, stop blaming the weather.
residents.fog: Fog at the pane. Keep the set dry. Invisible water is still water.
residents.night: Night outside. Keep a lamp where you can find it. The time to replace the flex is before it fails in the dark.

residents.cold: Cold at the window. I brought the heavy coat out, subject to the afternoon becoming less cold. It's on the chair provisionally.
residents.heat: Hot in here. I've removed my jacket. I mention it because I put it back on twice before you came.
residents.wet: Rain. An umbrella establishes an intention to go out, but doesn't oblige one to leave immediately. Mine is open by the door.
residents.snow: Snow at the pane. I was going to wait for it to stop. That isn't, strictly speaking, a plan for going out.
residents.clearing: It has stopped raining. There is no longer a weather-related reason to delay. I checked.
residents.fair: Fine outside. No grounds for postponement. Rather a severe sort of morning, when you put it that way.
residents.trend: It's been like this for days. At some point the weather becomes a condition of the errand, rather than a reason not to do it.
residents.fog: Fog. I can see the first lamp. That is sufficient for the first part of the walk, presumably.
residents.night: Dark at the window. The errand can wait until morning. That is a decision. I am trying to leave it as one.

residents.cold: Cold at the window. The scarf stays on until the room earns an entrance without it.
residents.heat: Heat. No breath left over for drama. A remarkably inconsiderate arrangement.
residents.wet: Rain at the pane. A beautifully attentive audience. Applauds everything, listens to nothing.
residents.snow: Snow outside. For once the street knows how to hold a silence. Don't praise it; you'll spoil it.
residents.clearing: The rain has finished. No bow. I could learn something from its exits.
residents.fair: Lovely light. Completely wrong angle for this face. I'll bear it.
residents.trend: The weather has kept the stage for days. I admire commitment. I'd admire an interval more.
residents.fog: Fog outside. Marvellous entrance for a roof. Nobody can see it and everyone knows it is there.
residents.night: The windows across the way are going out. A sensible audience knows when to go home. A sensible performer, too, apparently.

residents.cold: Cold light through the window. You can see every scratch on the glass. None of them is in the sky.
residents.heat: Heat in the room. Camera stays out of the sun. The shadow is doing useful work today.
residents.wet: Water on the pane. It changes the roofline if you move your head. The roof hasn't moved.
residents.snow: Snow outside. Less detail, more shape. I haven't taken a picture. Looking is allowed to be enough.
residents.clearing: A stripe of light after the rain. It won't stay. That doesn't make it late.
residents.fair: Good light. I'm trying leaving the camera on the table for a minute of it.
residents.trend: Same weather, several days. I've been looking from the same window. It isn't the same view.
residents.fog: Fog over the roofs. A soft edge is still an edge. I can wait for it to come back.
residents.night: The window is dark. The room is in the glass now. I can leave the camera on the table for that.

residents.cold: Cold by the window. Dry stockings first. Then you can tell me how little it bothers you.
residents.heat: Close in here. Sit down, have some water. Being busy isn't a substitute for either.
residents.wet: Rain at the glass. Put the wet coat down. You can tell the story while you're drying.
residents.snow: Snow. Warm your hands gently. I know the stove is quicker. Quicker isn't always kinder.
residents.clearing: Rain's stopped. Give the steps a chance to dry. A change in the sky doesn't remove water from stone.
residents.fair: Good light. If you've been meaning to go out, take some of it while it's there.
residents.trend: Several days of this. Check on the person who always says they're managing. Especially that person.
residents.fog: Fog today. Take your time on the steps. Being late is preferable to arriving hurt.
residents.night: Night outside. If there is nothing urgent, sit down. There will be enough urgent things in the morning.

residents.cold: Cold in by the window. They said the room was airy. An accurate description, for once.
residents.heat: Warm room. I packed the wrong things. That seems to be what packing is.
residents.wet: Rain. My coat's drying over there, so I suppose I'm staying another cup of tea.
residents.snow: Snow outside. I had a departure in mind. The snow has suggested I think about it again.
residents.clearing: Stopped raining. Now I have to decide whether I meant to leave or just meant to stop waiting.
residents.fair: Fine light at this window. You don't get that listed with the room.
residents.trend: Same weather for days. Funny how quickly you start calling somebody else's window your window.
residents.fog: Fog at this window. I have been promised a view. Evidently it comes at certain hours.
residents.night: The window has gone dark. I should put my things where I can find them. That makes it sound as though I live here.
